Looking at this situation:

- My cost of capital is 0.1447 APR - I lose money below this
- The auction has consistently cleared at 0.1126 APR, won by F0 every round
- F0 appears to be bidding very aggressively at or below 0.1126 APR, which is below my cost of capital
- In a second-price auction, I win if I bid lower than everyone else, but get paid the second-lowest bid

Since F0 keeps winning at 0.1126 APR (which is below my cost of capital of 0.1447), I cannot profitably undercut F0. If I bid below 0.1447, I'd lose money even in the best case. 

My optimal strategy is to bid my true value (cost of capital) at 0.1447. If somehow F0 drops out or bids higher, I might win and get paid the second price (which could be the reserve of 0.3000 or F0's bid). But realistically, F0 will continue to win.

Bidding at my cost of capital is the dominant strategy - it's truthful bidding in a second-price auction, and I won't win unprofitably.
